title: Well-founded induction on group order for Jordan-Holder uniqueness
intent: Prove Jordan-Holder uniqueness - that the factor lists of any two composition series of a finite group agree up to isomorphism and permutation - by well-founded induction on the group order #|G|, the inductive step assembled from ten named project lemmas: two base cases (trivg_comps, simple_compsP), an order decrease (maxnormal_proper), normality of the maximal subgroups (maxnormal_normal), the product lemma and the second isomorphism theorem (maxnormalM, weak_second_isog), a common refinement (exists_comps), simplicity of the quotients to feed the induction hypothesis (quotient_simple, isog_simple), and permutation assembly (section_repr_isog).

parent.name: JordanHolderUniqueness
parent.statement:
Lemma JordanHolderUniqueness (G : gTg) (s1 s2 : seq gTg) :
  comps G s1 -> comps G s2 -> perm_eq (mkfactors G s1) (mkfactors G s2).

children.name: trivg_comps
children.statement: Lemma trivg_comps G s : comps G s -> (G :==: 1) = (s == [::]).
children.closed_by: case/andP=> ls cs; apply/eqP/eqP (forward: rewrite s1; backward: case s => //= H s /andP[/maxgroupp], rewrite /proper sub1G andbF)

children.name: simple_compsP
children.statement: Lemma simple_compsP G s : comps G s -> reflect (s = [:: 1%G]) (simple G).
children.closed_by: apply: (iffP idP); uses trivg_comps, simpleP, simple_maxnormal, maxgroupp, maxgroupP

children.name: maxnormal_proper
children.statement: Lemma maxnormal_proper A B C : maxnormal A B C -> A \proper B.

children.name: maxnormalM
children.statement:
Lemma maxnormalM G H K :
  maxnormal H G G -> maxnormal K G G -> H :<>: K -> H * K = G.
children.closed_by: contraNeq then wlog on H \subset K; maxgroupP, normC, comm_joingE, normalM (uses maxnormal_normal internally)

children.name: weak_second_isog
children.statement: Lemma weak_second_isog : H / (K :&: H) \isog H * K / K.

children.name: exists_comps
children.statement: Lemma exists_comps (G : gTg) : exists s, comps G s.
children.closed_by: elim: {G} #|G| (well-founded induction on order); boolP (simple G), ex_maxnormal_ntrivg, maxnormal_proper

children.name: quotient_simple
children.statement:
Lemma quotient_simple gT (G H : {group gT}) :
  H <| G -> simple (G / H) = maxnormal H G G.

children.name: section_repr_isog
children.statement:
Lemma section_repr_isog s1 s2 :
  s1 \isog s2 -> section_repr s1 = section_repr s2.
children.closed_by: congr (odflt _ _); apply: eq_pick => s; apply: isog_transr

applicability.goal_shape: For two lists s1 s2 and a group G, an equality perm_eq (f s1) (f s2) (multiset equality up to permutation) under assumptions comps G s1 -> comps G s2; the induction is well-founded on the group order #|G| with the two series s1 s2 kept generalised (elim: n G ... in s1 s2 *).
applicability.use_when: the goal reduces to a strictly decreasing measure (here the group order), the base cases are a trivial and a simple object with a reflect characterisation lemma, and the step needs exactly: an order decrease to the maximal proper normal subgroups, a common refinement, two second-isomorphism quotients, simplicity of the quotients, and a permutation assembly.
applicability.avoid_when: the measure does not strictly decrease into the refined subgroup (then the IH cannot be applied), the base cases need bespoke arguments rather than a reflect characterisation, or the two series cannot share a common refinement so the permutation assembly has nothing to commute.

The same well-founded-induction-on-order skeleton is reused almost line-for-line for the action-invariant version StrongJordanHolderUniqueness in the same file (lines 575-660), which swaps the comps/maxnormal lemmas for their acomps/maxainv counterparts.

The main proof body spans 58 lines (167-224) and cites 10 named project lemmas directly (trivg_comps, simple_compsP, maxnormal_proper, maxnormal_normal, maxnormalM, weak_second_isog, exists_comps, quotient_simple, section_repr_isog, and isog_simple at lines 207 and 214); the longest chain of project lemmas below the main theorem that I checked has depth 2 (JordanHolderUniqueness -> exists_comps -> maxnormal_proper, and JordanHolderUniqueness -> simple_compsP -> trivg_comps).

consequences: The move creates the obligations the induction step must discharge: (a) the order decreases along each maximal normal subgroup (maxnormal_proper, lines 181-184), (b) a composition series exists for the common refinement N1 :&: N2 (exists_comps, line 200), (c) the two quotient isomorphisms (G / N1) ~= (N2 / N) and (G / N2) ~= (N1 / N) hold (maxnormalM + weak_second_isog, lines 193-199), and (d) the quotients are simple so the induction hypothesis applies (quotient_simple + isog_simple, lines 205-214). The generalisation must keep s1 s2 free across the induction (in s1 s2 *), and the base cases must be recognised by reflect lemmas (trivg_comps, simple_compsP). Failure mode: if the measure does not strictly decrease into the refinement N, the IH cannot be applied and the step stalls.
